references.text: In the parable of the minas, Jesus says: "Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very little, you shall have authority over ten cities." This directly illustrates the principle that faithfulness in small things leads to responsibility over greater things ([ref:Luk 19:17|Luke 19:17]).

In the parable of the talents, the Lord says: "Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much." The same principle applies: faithfulness in small things qualifies one for greater responsibility ([ref:Matt 25:21-23|Matthew 25:21-23]).

Jesus says that whoever sets aside even the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called the least in the kingdom of heaven. This shows that faithfulness even in small matters has significance for God's kingdom ([ref:Matt 5:19|Matthew 5:19]).
Paul writes that what is required of stewards is that they be found faithful. Faithfulness in stewardship is also a central theme in Luke 16:10 ([ref:1 Kor 4:2|1 Corinthians 4:2]).

The verses immediately following elaborate on the principle: If you have not been faithful with unrighteous wealth, who will entrust to you the true riches? And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own? ([ref:Luk 16:11-12|Luke 16:11-12]).

"Whoever goes about slandering reveals secrets, but he who is trustworthy in spirit keeps a thing covered." Proverbs links faithfulness with reliability regarding what has been entrusted to one ([ref:Ordsp 11:13|Proverbs 11:13]).
Daniel was faithful in his service, and his adversaries could find no fault or error in him. He stands as an example of faithfulness in what was entrusted to him ([ref:Dan 6:4|Daniel 6:4]).

"Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life." Jesus encourages the church in Smyrna to be faithful, which is also the foundational principle in Luke 16:10 ([ref:Åp 2:10|Revelation 2:10]).
Moses was faithful in all God's house. Faithfulness in what one has been entrusted is a consistent biblical principle that supports Jesus' words in Luke 16:10 ([ref:Hebr 3:2|Hebrews 3:2]).
The preceding verse speaks about using unrighteous wealth wisely and faithfully. Verse 10 summarizes the underlying principle from the parable of the unjust steward ([ref:Luk 16:9|Luke 16:9]).
